@sachindetrax binary: /home/bfg/applications/llama.cpp/build/bin/llama-server
model: BTL-4-IQ2_XXS.gguf

# mmproj: removed. Compact is a text-only build with no vision tower, and that
#   projector was for Qwen3.6 anyway. BTL-4 is qwen3_5_moe.
# chat_template: removed. The GGUF ships the correct one. BTL-4 uses a
#   <tool_call><function=name><parameter=x> DSL, not stock Qwen's JSON form.

host: 0.0.0.0
port: 8080
ui: false

# Use the GGUF's embedded Jinja template. Without this, llama.cpp falls back to
# its legacy built-in templates and BTL-4's tool-call format is never used, so
# removing the chat_template override above only helps if this is on.
jinja: true

# Separate reasoning into reasoning_content instead of letting it accumulate
# into content every turn. llama.cpp's default "auto" does not do this
# correctly for BTL-4.
reasoning_format: deepseek

threads: 6
threads_batch: 6

ubatch_size: 2048
batch_size: 2048

gpu_layers: 99
flash_attention: "on"
parallel: 1

@ctjlewis The model on the left is Qwen3-1.7B, not Opus. It obviously knows basic arithmetic. It actually found the correct expression at token 1,313, checked it several more times, then drifted back into bad ideas and never returned the answer. That is the behaviour the demo is showing.
Interference Search isn’t meant to teach a model that 4 × 4 = 16. The arithmetic on the search side is exact. The problem is choosing and composing operations without exploring the same effective state repeatedly. With six numbers, 831,176 possible paths collapsed into 13,229 distinct states. That is where the saving comes from.
I do agree that saying “models reason in a line” is too broad. Models clearly compile common operations into their weights. Call that memoization if you want. The interesting version of Interference Search would let those reliable operations remain atomic, then externalize the parts that still require search, merge equivalent outcomes, and remove dead states.
The 128-digit multiplication is cool, but it doesn’t really argue against any of that. It shows that a model can execute a long arithmetic procedure. It doesn’t show that combinatorial search, repeated states, and losing valid solutions have disappeared.
